key_insight: SolCloudLLM combines sky images and time-series in a bidirectional multimodal LLM framework to better forecast short-term PV power and GHI, especially when clouds drive rapid changes.
engineering_relevance: Improved cloud-aware solar forecasting can support more reliable dispatch, reserve scheduling, and grid operations at site-specific locations with limited training data.
method: Align sky-image patches with time-series patches.
Fuse both modalities through bidirectional multimodal fusion.
Map the unified representation into an LLM embedding space for forecasting.
evidence_signal: On SIRTA and SKIPP'D, the method outperformed all baselines in MSE across horizons, with up to 25.4% relative reduction, and showed the strongest gains under cloudy conditions and few-shot settings.
watch_item: Performance depends on site-specific data and image availability, so deployment may require careful calibration and robust handling of missing or low-quality sky imagery.
paper_title: Bidirectional Multimodal Fusion of Sky Images and Time-Series for Solar Forecasting with Large Language Models
